Prescribed Subject (same as SL) — a core area of History.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Prescribed Subject (same as SL) brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

mcqs.q: Which Bolshevik slogan summarised Lenin's April Theses?
options: Peace, Land, Bread
Workers of the world unite
Liberte, egalite, fraternite
Better dead than red

mcqs.q: What was the immediate cause of the February Revolution?
options: German invasion
Bread shortages in Petrograd
Lenin's return from Switzerland
Kerensky's offensive

mcqs.q: Why did the League of Nations fail to prevent WWII?
options: The League failed because no countries joined it.
The League failed because Hitler banned it in 1933.
Absence of the US, requirement of unanimous decisions, no armed force of its own, weak responses to Manchuria (1931) and Abyssinia (1935), and great-power self-interest.
The UN forced Britain to grant independence to all colonies in 1945.

mcqs.q: Why did the British Empire end after WWII?
options: The UN forced Britain to grant independence to all colonies in 1945.
Britain was bankrupted by the war, faced rising nationalist movements, and confronted US/Soviet pressure against colonialism in a new world order.
Britain voluntarily gave its colonies independence as a moral choice.
Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.

mcqs.q: Why did Stalin blockade West Berlin in 1948?
options: Stalin blockaded Berlin to stop Nazis escaping to the West.
To force the Western Allies out of Berlin in response to the merging of their zones, introduction of the Deutschmark, and creation of a separate West German state.
Stalin blockaded Berlin because he wanted to invade Western Europe.
The UN forced Britain to grant independence to all colonies in 1945.
